title: watchmen-handback-notes
body:
Purpose:
- Quick, portable handback for the night shift. Not a canonical runbook; scribbles + commands for the next oncall.

TL;DR (2 lines):
- If 5xx rate on /v1/generate > 1% or p95 latency > 500ms, run the triage flow below.
- If queue backlog > 5000 or batcher OOMs, enable temporary throttling and notify dedicated infra.

Pre-handoff checks (5 min):
- Slack: check #oncall and last 2 hours of alerts.
- Grafana quick panels: latency-50/95, errors-5xx, queue-length, gpu-util.
- K8s: kubectl -n inference-prod get pods -l tier=runtime --no-headers -o custom-columns=":metadata.name,:status.phase,:spec.nodeName"
- Pager status: confirm oncall rota and escalation phone numbers.

Symptoms worth immediate action:
- Rising 5xx across models (multiple routes) -> suspect runtime crash loop or kv-cache failure.
- Single-model p95 spike with steady pods -> queuing or model variant regression.
- High queue length + low GPU utilization -> batcher stuck or shard mismatch.

Quick triage flow (ordered):
1) Check cluster health
- kubectl -n inference-prod get svc,pods,deployments -l app=redwood -o wide
- kubectl top pods -n inference-prod | sort -k2 -n (look for pods with 0 CPU but high restarts)

2) Inspect batcher & queue
- kubectl logs deployment/batcher -n inference-prod --tail=200
- kubectl exec -n inference-prod deployment/batcher -- curl -s http://localhost:8080/metrics | egrep "queue_length|pending_requests"
- If queue_length > 1000: kubectl scale deploy/batcher --replicas=$((current+1)) OR enable temporary throttling (see Mitigations)

3) Check runtime pods & KV cache
- kubectl -n inference-prod get pods -l component=runtime -o wide
- kubectl logs pod/<pod> -n inference-prod -c runtime --since=15m | tail -n 200  (search for "cache miss" / "kv error")
- If KV cache errors: restart kv-sidecar on affected pods: kubectl rollout restart sts/kv-sidecar -n inference-prod (note: statefulset)

4) Look at gateway and proxy
- kubectl logs deployment/gateway -n inference-prod --tail=200
- If 502/504: check inference-proxy config and connection pool: kubectl exec -n inference-prod deploy/inference-proxy -- curl -s http://localhost:9000/status

Temporary mitigations (fast, reversible):
- Throttle new requests at API gateway: curl -X POST $GATEWAY_ADMIN/throttle -d '{"rate":0.6}'  (inform product about degraded mode)
- Enable small-batch mode: set ConfigMap inference-config -> batching.max_tokens=512 then kubectl rollout restart deployment/redwood-runtime -n inference-prod (fast restart, affects throughput)
- Short-term model fallback: change route to lighter model (if available) via console or patch: kubectl patch route/route-name -n infra --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/model","value":"redwood/mode-small-v2"}]'  (use only if acceptance tests were green)
- Restart sequence for noisy pod: kubectl delete pod <pod> -n inference-prod --grace-period=10 (will recycle, useful if state is stuck)

Escalation matrix (when to call people):
- If >30 min without resolution and customer-impacting: page SRE lead Marco Liu (pager) and CC engineering-duty channel.
- If suspected hardware/GPU failure: page infra-oncall and open a ticket with cloud provider.
- If leak/regression suspected (deploy in last 30m): page deploy-author and hold rollback PR.

Quick commands cheat-sheet:
- Check router errors: kubectl logs deploy/gateway -n inference-prod | egrep "5..|timeout" | tail -n 200
- Rollout restart runtime: kubectl rollout restart deployment/redwood-runtime -n inference-prod
- Force drain a node (careful): kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
- Check recent deploys: kubectl get rs -n inference-prod --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 10

Post-incident stub (write this before handing off):
- Incident summary (one para)
- Root cause hypothesis
- Mitigations applied with timestamps
- Who was paged / who triaged
- Next steps / followups assigned (Jira / owner)

Notes to self / heuristics:
- If GPUs sit <30% and queue is large: usually a batching/batcher issue, not model slowness.
- Bad quantization/format mismatch shows as sudden p50 increase but p95 stable.
- KV cache saturation: lots of cache-evict logs, sudden CPU spikes on kv pods.

Open questions (to add to proper runbook later):
- Where do we keep the canonical fallback-model map for each route? (should be in Confluence)
- Can we push a read-only, rate-limited public endpoint for internal smoke tests?

TODOs (low friction items to convert into tickets):
- Create a lightweight pager template for model fallback (OPS-128) - owner: Nina
- Add a small dashboard for batcher queue length in oncall glance (owner: Aisha)
- Document exact kv-sidecar restart steps and confirm no data loss (owner: Marco)

Micro-handoff checklist (what I will say when I hand to you):
1) "Two-line summary: we had a batcher stall earlier, I restarted batcher and throttled gateway to 60%. Currently errors are down to 0.3% and p95 ~ 420ms."
2) Key artifacts: logs copied to /tmp/oncall-dump-<ts>.tgz (ask me for the path).
3) Open followups: dashboard + OPS-128.

If you get a weird alert and are unsure: ping @aisha or drop a note in #oncall with the short TL;DR and timestamps.

End of notes. Keep this as your short-term pocket guide. If anything here helped, convert it to the proper runbook entry and link it in Confluence.
